rmt-2004-calc-03.title: Velocity and acceleration
rmt-2004-calc-03.body:
$v=20t^3-5t^4=5t^3(4-t)$ and $a=60t^2-20t^3=20t^2(3-t)$. The object slows down when $v$ and $a$ have opposite signs. $v>0$ for $0<t<4$ and $v<0$ for $t>4$; $a>0$ for $0<t<3$ and $a<0$ for $t>3$. They have opposite signs exactly for $3<t<4$.

**Answer: $3<t<4$**

rmt-2004-calc-05.title: Minimise the cost
rmt-2004-calc-05.body:
Let $x$ miles of old road be restored; the new road has length $\sqrt{9+(5-x)^2}$. Cost (in units of 200,000 dollars): $C(x)=x+2\sqrt{9+(5-x)^2}$ for $0\le x\le5$. $C'(x)=1-\frac{2(5-x)}{\sqrt{9+(5-x)^2}}=0$ gives, with $u=5-x$, $\sqrt{9+u^2}=2u$, so $3u^2=9$, $u=\sqrt3$ and $x=5-\sqrt3\approx3.27$. Check the endpoints: $C(0)=2\sqrt{34}\approx11.66$, $C(5)=5+6=11$, and $C(5-\sqrt3)=5-\sqrt3+4\sqrt3=5+3\sqrt3\approx10.20$, smaller than both endpoints.

**Answer: $5-\sqrt3$ miles**

rmt-2004-calc-06.title: Slopes
rmt-2004-calc-06.body:
Substituting $y=2x$: $x^2-2x^2+8x^2=7x^2=28$, so $x=\pm2$ and the points are $(2,4)$, $(-2,-4)$. The line has slope $m_1=2$. Differentiating $x^2-xy+2y^2=28$ implicitly: $2x-y-xy'+4yy'=0$, so $y'=\frac{y-2x}{4y-x}$, which is $0$ at both points. So the angle $\alpha$ between the curves satisfies $|\tan\alpha|=\left|\frac{m_2-m_1}{1+m_1m_2}\right|=\left|\frac{0-2}{1}\right|=2$.

**Answer: 2**

rmt-2004-calc-08.title: Integrate the force
rmt-2004-calc-08.body:
Let $h$ be the height the cow has been lifted, $0\le h\le100$. The cow plus water weighs $200-\frac h2$ and the chain still hanging weighs $2(100-h)$. The work is $\int_0^{100}\left(400-\frac52h\right)dh=40000-\frac52\cdot5000=27500$ foot-pounds.

**Answer: 27500**

rmt-2004-calc-09.title: Slice
rmt-2004-calc-09.body:
The parabolas meet where $y^2=3-2y^2$, i.e. $y=\pm1$, $x=1$. A slice at $x$ has side $s=2|y|$: $s=2\sqrt x$ for $0\le x\le1$ and $s=2\sqrt{\frac{3-x}2}$ for $1\le x\le3$. The area of an equilateral triangle is $\frac{\sqrt3}4s^2$, so $V=\int_0^1\sqrt3\,x\,dx+\int_1^3\frac{\sqrt3}2(3-x)\,dx=\frac{\sqrt3}2+\sqrt3=\frac{3\sqrt3}2$.

**Answer: $\frac{3\sqrt3}2$**
